subtitles.en: Is this just more signal that, you know, is this just going to continue to feel growth? Or do you think it's the opposite where we're just dealing with some very expensive bills coming up? Yeah.

subtitles.en: I mean, at the end of the day, it's about where do you feel about the AI cycle? Do you see GPU utilization improving? Do you see AI monetization improving?

subtitles.en: You know, all of this is critical for more investments in sims, more investment in capital spending, more investment in AI in front.

subtitles.en: Yeah, which is also raised the issue of, you know, how this is making the circular nature of the investing and, you know, inflating some of the demand for AI.

subtitles.en: But Felix, you raised an interesting point that could still be the idea of, you know, we're building more than we actually need. What is your sense of what the earliest warning indicators, I guess, will be to know that we are in that stage of the AI buildout.

subtitles.en: So by overbuilding, what I mean by that is you start seeing AI monetization really turn. subtitles.zh: 所谓过度建设，是指AI变现开始转向，比如AI增长、GPU利用率，或者GPU和CPU的租赁价格开始下滑，尤其是Blackwell和即将推出的Rubin芯片，这对整个AI生态建设不是好兆头。

subtitles.en: I mentioned earlier, you know, overbuilding, what if token growth is not 10X, 100X, what people are thinking the next five years, we have a really good read throughout token database, tracking about 800 LM models globally from both US and China.
subtitles.zh: 我之前提到，如果token增长不是人们预期的未来五年10倍、100倍呢？我们通过token数据库追踪全球约800个大模型，包括中美两国。

subtitles.en: So we keep a close eye on token growth to make sure, you know, it's at a good level to sustain higher and higher CAPEX spending and investment spending for the AI guys.

subtitles.en: So a lot of data out there that we can track to kind of gauge whether, you know, we could be sort of overbuilding at the top of the AI site going on, but I'm not saying that currently.

subtitles.en: I mean, we've been seeing it, you know, it's becoming a bit of under pressure, hopefully.
subtitles.zh: 我们一直在关注，英伟达股价确实面临一些压力。

subtitles.en: Yeah, today in particular, but look, I think, you know, when they report earnings, you can't just look at the typical revenues, margins, catbacks, figures anymore, you really need to dig deeper now.
subtitles.zh: 尤其是今天。但你看，当英伟达公布财报时，不能再只看常规的收入、利润率、回购这些数字了，需要更深入挖掘。

subtitles.en: and to say looking at accounts receivables, maybe into their investments, maybe looking into the, you know, the footnotes when they talk about commitments, contingencies, because now people are looking at Nvidia as a financing lender, right?
subtitles.zh: 要看应收账款、对外配置，还有脚注里的承诺和或有事项。因为现在市场把英伟达看作一个融资方。

subtitles.en: So this, all of these metrics now matter in understanding, you know, what are they going to do with their free cash flow?
subtitles.zh: 所以这些指标都很关键，能帮我们判断英伟达会如何运用自由现金流。

subtitles.en: How much investments they're going to make for third parties now? And by the way, their free cash flow is not infinite.
subtitles.zh: 他们会为第三方投入多少资金？而且，他们的自由现金流并非无限。

subtitles.en: Right now, you know, my model is around a hundred billion, and they're going around making a lot of deals that's higher than that, right?
subtitles.zh: 目前我的模型测算大约一千亿美元，但他们正在进行的交易规模远超这个数字。

subtitles.en: So people can worry, you know, how can Nvidia finance this? Well, they have to raise money.
subtitles.zh: 所以市场会担心英伟达如何为这些交易融资？答案是必须举债。

subtitles.en: All of this affects sentiment on the stock. But generally speaking, you know, we have a really good regression model to model Nvidia's data center revenues for the quarter and guidance has a ninety-seven percent on square.
subtitles.zh: 这些都会影响市场情绪。但总体而言，我们有一个很好的回归模型来预测英伟达数据中心季度收入，拟合度高达97%。

subtitles.en: And so far, you know, the AI trade continues to trend higher for Nvidia in terms of their Ruben demand and so forth.
subtitles.zh: 到目前为止，AI交易对英伟达的Rubin需求等仍在上升。

subtitles.en: However, I just came back from a memory storage conference out on the West Coast.
subtitles.zh: 不过，我刚从西海岸的一场存储大会回来。

subtitles.en: And they were talking about trying to reduce GPUs through innovations in memory architecture because GPUs, HBM, they've become too expensive.
subtitles.zh: 会上讨论通过内存架构创新来减少GPU用量，因为GPU和HBM太贵了。

subtitles.en: So that's also weighing on sentiment here on Nvidia. Interesting.
subtitles.zh: 这也在影响英伟达的市场情绪。确实值得关注。

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
